questions.question_text: Choose the correct option that best defines climate resilience.

options.A: The capacity of systems to cope with hazards while maintaining their core functions and the ability to adapt and transform
options.B: The process of preventing all climate-related disasters through strict environmental laws
options.C: The rapid recovery of economic systems after any natural event
options.D: The elimination of social and environmental vulnerability through technology

questions.explanation: Climate resilience refers to the ability of a system to absorb shocks and adapt while maintaining its essential structure and functions.

questions.question_text: Determine whether the following statement is True or False. Select one of the options listed to select your choice. Small enterprises are characterised by investments up to ₹125 crore and a turnover not exceeding ₹500 crore.

options.A: True
options.B: False
options.C: N/A
options.D: N/A

questions.explanation: The current classification for small enterprises in India is an investment up to ₹10 crore and turnover up to ₹50 crore.

questions.question_text: In a drought-prone village, local elders advise farmers to sow seeds only after observing the blooming of a particular wild plant which is a signal that underground moisture is sufficient for germination. A scientific team later confirms that this plant blooms only when soil humidity reaches a threshold ideal for seed growth. The government then decides to include this traditional indicator in official drought forecasting programs. Question: Which statement best explains the significance of this practice?

options.A: Indigenous knowledge reflects experiential understanding that can complement modern science when validated through observation and evidence.
options.B: Indigenous knowledge provides symbolic cultural traditions that have little scientific basis.
options.C: Indigenous knowledge is reliable only when replaced by modern scientific forecasting systems.
options.D: Indigenous knowledge functions independently of environmental observations and has no practical value.

questions.explanation: Traditional and indigenous knowledge provides valuable insights based on long-term observation that can enhance and complement modern scientific methods.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements best distinguishes climate mitigation from climate adaptation?

options.A: Climate mitigation focuses on adjusting to climate impacts, while climate adaptation works to stop greenhouse gas emissions.
options.B: Climate mitigation reduces the effects of climate change, while climate adaptation reduces the causes by cutting greenhouse gas emissions.
options.C: Climate mitigation reduces the causes of climate change, while climate adaptation manages its effects to minimize harm or seize opportunities.
options.D: Climate mitigation deals only with emergency response after disasters, while climate adaptation prevents emissions through technology.

questions.explanation: Mitigation focuses on addressing the root causes by reducing emissions, whereas adaptation focuses on managing the consequences of climate change.

questions.question_text: A popular shoe brand launches a new program where customers can return worn-out shoes. Instead of throwing them away, the company grinds the soles into new rubber, uses the fabric to make new uppers, and even repairs lightly used shoes for resale. This initiative reduces waste and the need for fresh raw materials. Which sustainability concept does this initiative represent?

options.A: Green Economy
options.B: Circular Economy
options.C: Linear Economy
options.D: Low- carbon Economy

questions.explanation: A circular economy aims to eliminate waste by continually reusing, repairing, and recycling resources within the production loop.

questions.question_text: In water-intensive sectors such as textiles, leather, and food processing, which strategy best promotes resource efficiency and long-term sustainability?

options.A: Increasing groundwater extraction to maintain production levels during dry seasons
options.B: Integrating rainwater harvesting, wastewater recycling, and periodic water audits into production systems
options.C: Relying on municipal water supply and focusing mainly on waste disposal measures
options.D: Using more freshwater for cleaning and processing to ensure higher product quality

questions.explanation: Resource efficiency in water-intensive industries is best achieved through recycling, harvesting, and regular monitoring to reduce overall consumption.

questions.question_text: Read the statement below and fill in the blank to complete the sentence meaningfully: ______________ was introduced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at COP26 in Glasgow on 1 November 2021 as a mass movement for mindful and deliberate utilization, instead of mindless and destructive consumption to protect and preserve the environment.

options.A: Lifestyle for Environment
options.B: Green India Mission
options.C: Clean Energy Initiative
options.D: Sustainable Living Plan

questions.explanation: LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) is an initiative launched by India to encourage sustainable living and mindful resource consumption.

questions.question_text: An MSME involved in electronic repairs aims to enhance its environmental image while complying with sustainability norms. Which of the following actions best represents responsible e-waste management?

options.A: Selling discarded electronic components to local recyclers without verifying their authorization status
options.B: Partnering with certified e-waste recyclers to ensure safe, traceable, and compliant disposal
options.C: Reusing damaged parts in new products to minimize waste, even if they fail to meet quality standards
options.D: Donating obsolete electronic parts to informal repair workshops for extended use

questions.explanation: Responsible management involves using certified channels to ensure that electronic waste is handled according to environmental and safety regulations.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes the changing business environment for MSMEs?

options.A: It focuses only on lowering production costs and increasing output.
options.B: It is increasingly shaped by sustainability goals, green supply chains, and consumer demand for eco-friendly products.
options.C: It ignores environmental standards and emphasizes traditional manufacturing.
options.D: It restricts MSMEs from accessing international markets due to sustainability norms.

questions.explanation: The modern business landscape for MSMEs is evolving to prioritize sustainability, green procurement, and environmentally conscious consumer preferences.

questions.question_text: Determine whether the following statement is True or False. Select one of the options listed to select your choice. In India, Small and Medium Enterprises are formally recognized as MSMEs under the MSME Act of 2006, which has largely remained unchanged since its introduction, with the most recent updates implemented in 2020 to reflect post-pandemic recovery needs.

options.A: True
options.B: False
options.C: N/A
options.D: N/A

questions.explanation: The MSME Act of 2006 governs the sector, and significant updates to definitions and criteria were indeed made in 2020.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements best describes how stakeholder mapping contributes to effective strategy implementation?

options.A: Stakeholder mapping is mainly used to outline internal communication channels without affecting strategic decisions.
options.B: Stakeholder mapping identifies key stakeholders, their interests, and engagement needs, enabling collaboration that strengthens strategic outcomes.
options.C: Stakeholder mapping identifies key stakeholders and their interests but has limited impact on the effectiveness of strategy execution.
options.D: Stakeholder mapping becomes relevant only after a strategy fails or encounters resistance.

questions.explanation: Stakeholder mapping helps identify those affected by or influencing a strategy, ensuring their engagement and alignment with organizational goals.

questions.question_text: Determine whether the following statement is True or False. Select one of the options listed to select your choice. Decarbonisation is a short-term initiative focused primarily on temporary reductions in fossil-fuel use, without requiring major changes in energy sources or process redesign.

options.A: True
options.B: False
options.C: N/A
options.D: N/A

questions.explanation: Decarbonisation is a long-term, systemic transition that requires fundamental changes to energy systems and industrial processes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not one of the Panchamrit commitments?

options.A: Achieving 500 GW of non-fossil energy capacity by 2030
options.B: Meeting 50 % of India’s energy requirements from renewable sources by 2030
options.C: Introducing a national carbon tax as part of climate policy by 2030
options.D: Reducing the carbon intensity of the economy by 45 % by 2030

questions.explanation: The Panchamrit commitments focus on capacity, intensity, and net-zero goals; a specific national carbon tax was not part of the initial five pillars.

questions.question_text: A mid-sized consulting firm operates out of a busy corporate office with dozens of workstations, constantly running servers, frequent client travel, and a heavy reliance on printed documents. The firm wants to start reducing its carbon footprint but cannot commit large upfront investments. Which option represents the most viable path for the firm to initiate decarbonisation efforts?

options.A: Prioritising a complete overhaul of office interiors with eco-labelled furniture and postponing energy-related upgrades to a later phase
options.B: Procuring renewable electricity, shifting to energy-efficient equipment, and moving paperwork and workflows to digital platforms to cut immediate energy and material use
options.C: Maintaining current energy systems but compensating emissions entirely through staff-led tree-planting drives and voluntary carbon-offset contributions
options.D: Reducing business travel while increasing on-site working hours to optimise office energy use without altering existing equipment or procurement patterns

questions.explanation: Improving efficiency through digitalization and renewable energy procurement offers immediate carbon reductions with manageable investment for service firms.

questions.question_text: __________ refers to achieving a balance between the greenhouse gases released into the atmosphere and those that are removed or absorbed.

options.A: net zero
options.B: carbon neutrality
options.C: emission balance
options.D: climate parity

questions.explanation: Net zero is the state where the amount of greenhouse gas emitted is equal to the amount removed from the atmosphere.

questions.question_text: A mid-sized food processing SME has identified multiple sources of emissions. It operates diesel powered delivery vehicles, purchases electricity from a coal-based grid, and sources packaging materials from an external supplier whose production process generates significant emissions. Which category of emissions is correctly matched to the activities of the enterprise?

options.A: Diesel burned in delivery vehicles is Scope 3, electricity purchased from the grid is Scope 1, and supplier-related emissions are Scope 2
options.B: Diesel burned in delivery vehicles is Scope 1, electricity purchased from the grid is Scope 2, and supplier-related emissions are Scope 3
options.C: Diesel burned in delivery vehicles is Scope 2, electricity purchased from the grid is Scope 3, and supplier-related emissions are Scope 1
options.D: Diesel burned in delivery vehicles is Scope 1, electricity purchased from the grid is Scope 3, and supplier-related emissions are Scope 2

questions.explanation: Scope 1 covers direct emissions, Scope 2 covers indirect emissions from purchased electricity, and Scope 3 includes all other indirect value chain emissions.

questions.question_text: Determine whether the following statement is True or False. Select one of the options listed to select your choice. GRI Standards are issued by SEBI in India and are mandatory for all companies under the BRSR framework.

options.A: True
options.B: False
options.C: N/A
options.D: N/A

questions.explanation: GRI Standards are international reporting frameworks; SEBI issues the BRSR framework specifically for Indian listed companies.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct option that best explains why different sectors require different decarbonisation pathways.

options.A: Because most sectors generate emissions through broadly similar activities, and applying one standardised strategy reduces complexity and improves consistency
options.B: Because sectors such as manufacturing, retail, logistics, construction, and services operate with different emission profiles, resource dependencies, and technological constraints that influence how decarbonisation must be approached
options.C: Because service-oriented sectors do not have meaningful carbon footprints, making decarbonization necessary only for energy-intensive industries
options.D: Because the success of decarbonization is determined primarily by government regulation, leaving operational differences between sectors largely irrelevant

questions.explanation: Emission reduction strategies must be sector-specific because each industry faces unique operational challenges and technological limitations.

questions.question_text: Reporting enables SMEs to build ______________ by demonstrating that they are responsibly managing environmental risks and aligning with sustainability expectations.

options.A: competitive visibility
options.B: trust and transparency
options.C: regulatory assurance
options.D: stakeholder compliance

questions.explanation: Transparency in reporting fosters trust among stakeholders, including investors and customers, regarding a company's environmental impact.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements best describes the role of SBTi?

options.A: It provides companies with voluntary sustainability disclosures that highlight environmental commitments without requiring alignment with climate science
options.B: It helps companies set greenhouse gas reduction targets that are consistent with climate science and aligned with the goals of the Paris Agreement
options.C: It sets general environmental guidelines for businesses that focus mainly on improving corporate image rather than meeting scientific benchmarks
options.D: It focuses exclusively on creating carbon offset projects for large multinational corporations

questions.explanation: The Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) ensures that corporate carbon reduction targets are scientifically rigorous and support global temperature limits.

questions.question_text: Which statement best explains climate adaptation for SMEs?

options.A: It refers to actions taken only after climate risks disrupt business operations and require urgent response
options.B: It involves forward-looking adjustments, including technological, operational, and ecological strategies to prepare for future climate risks
options.C: It primarily means purchasing external insurance protection against extreme weather events and natural disasters
options.D: It focuses on reducing emissions through carbon credits and offsetting rather than changing business practices

questions.explanation: Adaptation is a proactive approach involving adjustments to operations and strategies to reduce vulnerability to future climate impacts.

questions.question_text: A small manufacturing enterprise is exploring ways to reduce climate-related risks. However, the owner cannot secure affordable loans, lacks the technical expertise to assess suitable machinery upgrades and is unsure how to access available government support schemes. Which set of interventions would enable the SME overcome barriers to climate adaptation?

options.A: A mandate requiring SMEs to adopt climate-resilient technologies without providing any financial or technical support
options.B: Access to affordable finance, technical guidance on suitable technologies, and government incentives
options.C: Access to technical know-how on suitable technologies and information on government schemes
options.D: Waiting until climate risks disrupt operations and then applying for emergency relief schemes

questions.explanation: Overcoming adaptation barriers requires a combination of financial support, technical knowledge, and institutional incentives.

questions.question_text: If an SME prioritises measures such as backup power systems and emergency recovery plans, it can remain climate-secure even without adopting long-term strategies such as resource-efficient technologies or redesigned supply chains. Determine whether the statement is True or False.

options.A: True
options.B: False
options.C: N/A
options.D: N/A

questions.explanation: Short-term recovery plans do not provide long-term climate security; structural changes in resource use and supply chains are essential.

questions.question_text:
A millet-processing SME is facing repeated crop losses due to delayed monsoons, heatwaves, and rising

irrigation costs. Retail partners are demanding reliable supply, but farmers in the SME’s network are

struggling to maintain yields and incomes. The SME considers four strategies:

A. Invest in deeper borewells and high-capacity pumps to ensure irrigation even during heatwaves.

B. Shift to heat-resilient millet varieties, adopt sensor-based drip irrigation, and use weather advisory

systems to plan sowing.

C. Maintain current crop practices but secure climate insurance and short-term grain imports to meet supply

commitments.

D. Introduce drought-tolerant crops and provide insurance coverage, without changing irrigation or farming

methods.

Which option best represents the strongest long-term climate adaptation strategy for the SME?

options.A: Invest in deeper borewells and high-capacity pumps to ensure irrigation even during heatwaves.
options.B: Shift to heat-resilient millet varieties, adopt sensor-based drip irrigation, and use weather advisory systems to plan sowing.
options.C: Maintain current crop practices but secure climate insurance and short-term grain imports to meet supply commitments.
options.D: Introduce drought-tolerant crops and provide insurance coverage, without changing irrigation or farming methods.

questions.explanation: Using resilient crop varieties and water-efficient irrigation technology represents a holistic and sustainable long-term adaptation strategy.

questions.question_text: Determine whether the following statement is True or False. For SMEs in the EV ecosystem, recycling used batteries is sufficient to ensure both environmental adaptation and economic resilience, as it eliminates the need for second-life battery applications and mineral recovery systems.

options.A: True
options.B: False
options.C: N/A
options.D: N/A

questions.explanation: A resilient EV ecosystem requires more than just recycling; it must include comprehensive mineral recovery and second-life battery use to be truly sustainable.

questions.question_text: The ability of an SME to withstand disruptions such as floods, heatwaves, or supply chain failures while continuing operations is referred to as __________.

options.A: resilience
options.B: mitigation
options.C: adaptation
options.D: sustainability

questions.explanation: Resilience is the specific ability to persist and maintain core functions despite external shocks and disruptions.

questions.question_text:
A mid-sized packaging enterprise supplies printed cartons to three large FMCG brands. During a severe

heatwave, the industrial zone where all three suppliers operate faced rolling power cuts for over a week. Two

competitors had to stop production entirely. This enterprise however, quickly shifted part of its printing

operations to a rented facility in a neighbouring district and sourced board material from a backup supplier.

As a result, it delivered all orders on schedule. Three weeks later, one FMCG client renewed its annual

contract into a 3-year agreement and shortened the payment cycle from 60 to 30 days.

Which of the following best explains why the FMCG client improved contract terms for the SME?

options.A: The SME offered limited pricing adjustments during the disruption, making its products temporarily more commercially attractive than competitors
options.B: The SME maintained basic compliance and standard operating procedures, demonstrating that it could function without major structural changes during climate stress
options.C: The SME showed it could sustain on-time deliveries by rapidly shifting production and sourcing when competitors were forced to halt operations
options.D: The SME prioritised regulatory and documentation requirements, which reassured the client that contractual obligations would be formally fulfilled

questions.explanation: Demonstrated operational resilience and reliability during a crisis build high levels of trust and commercial value for buyers.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the best example of resilience in an SME?

options.A: Changing product design to reduce carbon emissions over the next 10 years
options.B: Continuing operations during a flood by using backup suppliers and trained staff
options.C: Waiting for government relief before restarting production after a heatwave
options.D: Focusing only on demand forecasting and ignoring climate disruptions

questions.explanation: Maintaining operations through the use of backup systems and prepared staff during an active hazard is a hallmark of resilience.

questions.question_text: Why is it important for SMEs to integrate both adaptation and resilience into their climate strategies instead of relying on only one of them?

options.A: Because adaptation ensures quick recovery after disruptions, while resilience focuses on long-term structural changes
options.B: Because adaptation reduces exposure to future risks, while resilience enables businesses to continue operating during shocks, making both necessary for comprehensive protection
options.C: Because resilience alone can fully prevent climate-related damage if supported by insurance schemes
options.D: Because adaptation and resilience are interchangeable approaches that eventually lead to the same outcomes

questions.explanation: Adaptation and resilience work together to minimize future risks and ensure immediate operational survival during crises.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best explains how environmental clauses from international buyers are transforming Indian SME operations?

options.A: They primarily require SMEs to publish CSR reports, but do not affect production or sourcing decisions
options.B: They focus only on carbon reporting, allowing SMEs to maintain existing machinery and energy systems
options.C: They require SMEs to modify procurement, energy use, production processes, and documentation practices to meet verifiable sustainability expectations
options.D: They affect only large firms, while SMEs are exempt from sustainability audits and contract level compliance

questions.explanation: International buyers demand rigorous compliance and verifiable sustainability practices across the entire value chain of their suppliers.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best reflects the aim of India’s National Wind–Solar Hybrid Policy?

options.A: To promote large renewable projects by expanding solar parks without integrating wind systems
options.B: To develop large grid-connected renewable projects that combine wind and solar power for better efficiency
options.C: To create large grid-connected renewable projects by scaling up solar parks alongside wind installations, without requiring hybrid integration
options.D: To shift investment away from hybrid systems and focus only on standalone solar development

questions.explanation: The hybrid policy promotes the integration of wind and solar power to optimize land use and improve the efficiency of the power grid.

questions.question_text: Which interpretation most accurately reflects the pattern of climate reporting in Asia as discussed in Module 4?

options.A: Climate reporting tends to intensify when governments announce long-term climate frameworks, since such policy documents dominate the environmental news cycle in most Asian outlets
options.B: Climate coverage surges predominantly during extreme weather calamities or high-visibility global summits, revealing an episodic and event-driven pattern of reporting rather than sustained climate journalism
options.C: Climate stories appear consistently throughout the year because Asian media maintain dedicated climate desks that ensure continuous coverage of slow-onset environmental changes
options.D: Climate attention often diminishes during severe environmental crises, as newsrooms reallocate space to political negotiations and sectoral economic updates

questions.explanation: Media coverage of climate in Asia is frequently reactive, spiking during disasters or summits rather than providing consistent, long-term reporting.

questions.question_text: The UNFCCC refers to Climate Change adaptation as changes in

options.A: Policy, practices, and structures
options.B: Processes, policy, and structures
options.C: Processes, practices, and structures
options.D: Practices, policies, and structures

questions.explanation: The UNFCCC definition emphasizes adjustments in processes, practices, and structures to address climate change impacts.

questions.question_text: Determine whether the following statement is True or False. According to the author of the book – Media and Climate Change: Making Sense of Press Narratives - the challenge for developing nations like India is to establish links between development and climate keeping the MDGs as framework to enhance the transition toward a low-carbon economy.

options.A: True
options.B: False
options.C: N/A
options.D: N/A

questions.explanation: Bridging developmental priorities with climate action is a key focus for media narratives and policy in developing countries like India.

questions.question_text: Determine whether the following statement is True or False. The UNFCCC is the primary international intergovernmental forum for negotiating the global response to climate change.

options.A: True
options.B: False
options.C: N/A
options.D: N/A

questions.explanation: The UNFCCC serves as the main global framework for international climate treaties and negotiations.

questions.question_text: _________________ is the United Nations body for assessing the science related to climate change.

options.A: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)
options.B: United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)
options.C: World Meteorological Organization (WMO)
options.D: Green Climate Fund (GCF)

questions.explanation: The IPCC is the leading international body for the assessment of climate change science.

questions.question_text: Based on the arguments presented in the book - Media and Climate Change: Making Sense of Press Narratives, which interpretation best explains why vulnerable communities affected by climate change in India remain largely absent from mainstream media narratives?

options.A: Because the media primarily functions as a neutral historical record, and its limited engagement with disadvantaged groups simply reflects their minimal role in broader public discourse
options.B: Because political influences on media organisations encourage reliance on official narratives, while disadvantaged groups despite their environmental proximity remain excluded due to lack of access to digitisation
options.C: Because communities closest to the environment tend to hold only traditional knowledge that cannot be integrated into contemporary climate communication frameworks
options.D: Because public interpretation of climate news depends mainly on consumer trends, making inclusion of marginalised communities unnecessary for shaping climate narratives

questions.explanation: Media narratives are often constrained by official viewpoints and lack of digital access for marginalized communities, excluding their perspectives from the discourse.

questions.question_text: Which underlying factor explains why firms with long-standing dependence on plastics and fossil-fuel models hesitate to transition toward sustainability?

options.A: Reluctance to experiment with new technologies, which creates slow and uneven innovation across the sector
options.B: A deeply entrenched focus on short-term financial gains, which often overrides commitments to broader People–Planet–Profit objectives
options.C: Regulatory pressure pushing companies to adopt sustainability measures more quickly than market conditions allow
options.D: Increasing consumer demand for sustainable alternatives, which reduces incentives for companies to maintain traditional production practices

questions.explanation: The prioritization of short-term profits over long-term sustainability goals often hinders the transition away from fossil-fuel-dependent models.

questions.question_text: The ‘+’ in REDD+ stands for

options.A: additional forest-related activities that protect the climate
options.B: additional area-related activities that protect the climate
options.C: additional climate-related activities that protect the forest
options.D: additional climate-related activities that protect the area

questions.explanation: The '+' in REDD+ refers to the role of conservation, sustainable management of forests, and enhancement of forest carbon stocks.

questions.question_text:
A Bengaluru-based start-up manufactures premium cold-pressed juices sold through e-commerce and cafes.

Until now, the company has used durable plastic bottles because they are cheap, lightweight, and convenient for long-distance delivery. However, three new developments create pressure:

· Delivery apps introduce a “sustainable choice” badge, and products packaged in plastics do not qualify.

· Urban Gen Z customers on social media are increasingly criticising brands that advertise “natural” products while using plastic packaging.

· The Karnataka government announces that it is considering state-level restrictions on certain single-use plastics within the next 18 months.

The founder wants to protect the brand’s image without causing a sudden cost spike that would force juice prices to go up and drive away customers in a competitive market.

Which of the following actions best represents a balanced approach?

options.A: Replace all plastic bottles immediately with premium glass packaging, signalling strong environmental intent even if logistics become more expensive and operationally difficult
options.B: Introduce recyclable or compostable packaging in selected high-volume products first, test cost and customer response, and phase out current plastics in a planned manner
options.C: Keep existing plastic packaging until regulations legally mandate a change, then carry out a full switch to whichever alternative seems cheapest at that time
options.D: Shift to glass or aluminium packaging for a few niche products only, but continue marketing all products as “eco-friendly” to maintain brand perception without major operational changes

questions.explanation: A phased approach allows a company to manage costs and evaluate market viability while working toward sustainability goals.
